# Sampling distributions {#sec-sampling}

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal"}
Code in this chapter uses **Julia**.
:::

If we repeatedly draw samples of size $n$ and compute $\bar{x}$ each time,
the collection of $\bar{x}$ values has its own distribution: the
**sampling distribution** of the mean. Its standard deviation is
$\sigma/\sqrt{n}$.

```{julia}
#| label: sim-means
using Distributions, Random, Statistics

Random.seed!(2026)
pop = Exponential(1.0)          # a right-skewed population, σ = 1
n, reps = 30, 10_000
xbars = [mean(rand(pop, n)) for _ in 1:reps]

(mean = mean(xbars), sd = std(xbars), theory_sd = 1 / sqrt(n))
```

The simulated standard deviation is close to the theoretical value
$1/\sqrt{30} \approx 0.183$. To *see* the distribution change as $n$ grows,
try the interactive app in @sec-interactive-clt.

## Exercises

1. Change `n` to 5 and to 100. How does the standard deviation of `xbars`
   change?
